summary: Extends the re-presentation approach beyond code to prose and research output: extract atomic claims, verify citations in a pipeline (DOI resolution, bibliographic matching, LLM relevance check), keep a numeric registry of computed values, and read a structured summary before the full text. Then gives staged recommendations: this week cap units at ~200 LOC and sessions at 60-90 minutes, require self-explanation blocks, name a human of record; this quarter move to spec-driven review, add an adversarial second-model pass plus package validation and security scanning, tier by risk; ongoing, auto-generate summaries and diagrams and track churn/duplication against a human baseline. Closes with thresholds that trigger tighter review and caveats about vendor sources, 2006-era limits, correlational trends, and preprint status.

claims.text: Hallucinated legal citations have produced sanctions in more than a thousand tracked cases worldwide
AI redundancy ran ~1.87x human levels in the MSR 2026 study
Post-merge defect or churn above ~1.5x the human baseline should trigger full line-by-line review and smaller chunks
claims.anchor: Recommendations > Thresholds that change the plan (L25)

claims.text: Approval faster than ~300-500 LOC/hour should be treated as rubber-stamping
claims.anchor: Recommendations > Thresholds that change the plan (L25)

claims.text: The 200-400 LOC and 60-90 minute figures come from 2006 human-written-code data and have not been re-derived for AI diffs
GitClear churn/duplication trends are correlational, not causal
The EASE 2026 64.53% figure merges evaluative feedback with workflow acknowledgments, so it is not a pure measure of substantive review
SmartBear, CodeRabbit, Qodo, and GitClear are vendor sources with commercial interest

risks.note: 'More than a thousand tracked cases' names no tracker or database.

risks.anchor: Recommendations > Thresholds that change the plan (L25)
risks.note: The 1.5x and 300-500 LOC/hour thresholds are author-chosen and not tied to a study; 300-500 differs from the 450 figure cited earlier.
A whitelist of computed values is proposed without evidence it catches errors in practice.

least_confident: Whether the citation-verification pipeline (CrossRef/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar plus LLM relevance check) reflects an existing tool or is the author's proposal; the chunk does not say.
